title: ～そうだ — appearance (“looks ～”)
summary: Says that something looks like ～ judging from its appearance. Attach そうだ to a verb stem or the stem of an i- or na-adjective. It can also mean “about to happen”, as in 雨が降りそうだ.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形の語幹＋そうだ
patterns.gloss: Verb stem + そうだ (降りそうだ / 壊れそうだ)
Adjective stem + そうだ (おいしそうだ)

body.p: For i-adjectives drop い (おいしい → おいしそう); いい → よさそう and ない → なさそう. Verbs take the stem.

It describes the speaker’s impression from looking, so it is not used for something you have already tasted. It does not attach to nouns or past facts. To pass on information heard, use the hearsay そうだ instead.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）はおいしそうです。
空（そら）が暗（くら）い。今（いま）にも雨（あめ）が降（ふ）りそうだ。
examples.romaji: Sora ga kurai. Ima ni mo ame ga furisō da.
examples.tr: The sky is dark. It looks like it will rain any moment.

examples.ja: この椅子（いす）は古（ふる）くて、壊（こわ）れそうだ。
examples.romaji: Kono isu wa furukute, kowaresō da.
examples.tr: This chair is old and looks like it will break.

pitfalls: いい → よさそう, ない → なさそう (not いそう).
Do not use it for facts you have already confirmed.
